{{Short description|Theorems about certain polynomial families}}
In mathematics, '''Turán's inequalities''' are some inequalities for [[Legendre polynomials]] found by Pál Turán<ref>{{Cite journal|title=On the zeros of the polynomials of Legendre|url=https://dml.cz/handle/10338.dmlcz/123879|journal=Časopis pro pěstování matematiky a fysiky|date=1950|issn=1802-114X|pages=113–122|volume=075|issue=3|doi=10.21136/CPMF.1950.123879|language=cs|first=Paul|last=Turan|doi-access=free}}</ref> (and first published by {{harvtxt|Szegö|1948}}<ref>{{Cite journal|title=On an inequality of P. Turán concerning Legendre polynomials|url=https://www.ams.org/bull/1948-54-04/S0002-9904-1948-09017-6/|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|date=1948|issn=0273-0979|pages=401–405|volume=54|issue=4|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1948-09017-6|language=en|first=G.|last=Szegö|doi-access=free}}</ref>). There are many generalizations to other polynomials, often called Turán's inequalities, given by {{harvs|mr=0040487
|last=Beckenbach|first= E. F.|last2= Seidel|first2= W.|last3= Szász|first3= Otto
|title=Recurrent determinants of Legendre and of ultraspherical polynomials
|journal=Duke Math. J.|volume= 18|year=1951|pages= 1–10}}<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Recurrent determinants of Legendre and of ultraspherical polynomials|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/duke-mathematical-journal/volume-18/issue-1/Recurrent-determinants-of-Legendre-and-of-ultraspherical-polynomials/10.1215/S0012-7094-51-01801-7.full|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|date=1951-03-01|issn=0012-7094|volume=18|issue=1|doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-51-01801-7|first=E. F.|last=Beckenbach|first2=W.|last2=Seidel|first3=Otto|last3=Szász|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and other authors.

If <math>P_n</math> is the <math>n</math>th [[Legendre polynomial]], Turán's inequalities state that
:<math>\,\! P_n(x)^2 > P_{n-1}(x)P_{n+1}(x)\ \text{for}\ -1<x<1.</math>


For <math>H_n</math>, the <math>n</math>th [[Hermite polynomial]], Turán's inequalities are
:<math>H_n(x)^2 - H_{n-1}(x)H_{n+1}(x)= (n-1)!\cdot \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\frac{2^{n-i}}{i!}H_i(x)^2>0 ,</math>

whilst for [[Chebyshev polynomials]] they are
:<math>T_n(x)^2 - T_{n-1}(x)T_{n+1}(x)= 1-x^2>0 \ \text{for}\ -1<x<1 .</math>
